A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with CoPA-Merging renamed RobustMerge. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains complete Appendices A–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original multimodal and vision experiments in Tables 2–5, together with component ablations and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds singular-vector diagnostics, layer-wise spectral analyses, and DoRA merging results.

M1.justification: CoPA-Merging becomes RobustMerge, but Equations 1–5 and Algorithm 1 retain magnitude pruning, complementary scaling, cross-task normalization, and additive merging. The DoRA experiment does not document a new merging component or procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight seen and four unseen multimodal tasks, POPE/MME/MMBench, and eight vision datasets. MM-MergeBench names the existing benchmark, and REC corresponds to the existing grounding task. DoRA changes model configuration, not task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in corresponding multimodal and vision comparisons. The added DoRA experiment uses the already evaluated Task Arithmetic and Ties-merging; newly cited PEFT methods do not become additional merging baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds a DoRA evaluation setting and diagnostic procedures measuring singular-vector similarity and singular-value ratios, separating the largest component from the remaining components. These extend evaluation within retained tasks; newly disclosed training and inference settings do not establish changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: v1's larger-half singular-value retention test is replaced by original-versus-pruned spectra in v2 Figure 3a. v2 additionally tests direction preservation with pruning/scaling controls in Figure 7, spectral behavior across layers in Appendix B, and robustness across PEFT techniques using DoRA. The task-count study is retained in Appendix F.

E5.justification: The standard-deviation comparison is retained unchanged from v1 Figure 6c to v2 Figure 5c. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2–7 retain their numerical results after matching renamed methods and reordered columns. v2 adds substantial spectral and direction-similarity findings and a DoRA result set: Table 9 reports averages of 56.08 for RobustMerge, 55.42 for Task Arithmetic, and 54.57 for Ties-merging. The earlier half-spectrum retention results are removed.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds a mathematical account absent from v1: SVD expansions, pairing of singular components across tasks, and a simplified two-model derivation interpreting merging as vector addition. Its reasoning relies on assumptions about corresponding components and similar left singular vectors; it is not a general performance proof.

C1.justification: The main claims about training-free merging, seen-task performance, and unseen-task generalization remain. v2 newly makes an explicit first-attempt claim for approaching parameter-efficient merging through direction robustness, while retaining the reported headline improvements.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's direction-preservation rationale, v2 develops interpretations of head-versus-tail instability, separate pruning/scaling effects, layer depth, and DoRA generalization. It also adds limitations concerning untested architectures/tasks and explains that directly operating on decomposed matrices remains future work.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability link and substantial reproduction information in Appendices C–E: LoRA placement, one training epoch, encoder freezing, lambda=2, temperature=0, a single NVIDIA A6000, vision inference procedures, and dataset-specific instruction templates. These are newly disclosed details, not demonstrated changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including DoRA, PiSSA, HiDe-LLaVA, and checkpoint/layer merging research, with limited accompanying discussion. The existing comparison with traditional merging approaches remains, supplemented by the direction-robustness novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, motivation, and conclusion are substantially revised around RobustMerge and direction robustness. Experimental setup subsections are consolidated, ablation and analysis sections are combined, and the task-count discussion moves to Appendix F. Terminology and grammar are edited throughout.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout with extensively reformatted tables and figures. v2 adds a direction-robustness diagram, diagnostic plots, instruction-template and DoRA tables; replaces the original Figure 2a; and relocates the task-count figure to the appendix.

improvement.justification: The new direction-similarity diagnostics provide more direct evidence for the proposed mechanism, while Appendices C/E supply previously missing training, inference, and prompt details. The DoRA experiment also strengthens validation. These improve assessability and reproducibility, although the main benchmark evidence is unchanged and Appendix A remains a simplified theoretical argument.
